column1: In late 1946 or early 1947, three Bedouin teenagers were tending their goats and sheep near the ancient settlement of Qumran, located on the northwest shore of the Dead Sea in what is now known as the West Bank.
column2: 1946年末或1947年初，三个贝都因少年在昆兰古聚落附近放牧山羊和绵羊。那里位于死海西北岸，属于今天所称的约旦河西岸地区。

column1: One of these young shepherds tossed a rock into an opening on the side of a cliff and was surprised to hear a shattering sound.
column2: 其中一名小牧人把一块石头扔进悬崖侧面的洞口，意外地听到一声碎裂的声响。

column1: He and his companions later entered the cave and stumbled across a collection of large clay jars, seven of which contained scrolls with writing on them.
column2: 后来，他和同伴进入山洞，偶然发现了一批大陶罐，其中七个罐里装着写有文字的卷轴。

column1: The teenagers took the seven scrolls to a nearby town where they were sold for a small sum to a local antiquities dealer.
column2: 少年们把七卷文书带到附近的镇上，以很低的价钱卖给了当地一名古董商。

column1: Word of the find spread, and Bedouins and archaeologists eventually unearthed tens of thousands of additional scroll fragments from 10 nearby caves; together they make up between 800 and 900 manuscripts.
column2: 发现古卷的消息传开后，贝都因人和考古学家又陆续从附近十座山洞中挖出数以万计的古卷残片。将这些材料合在一起，共有八百至九百份手稿。
column3: Word of the find|有关这次发现的消息
column6: tens of thousands of|数以万计的

column1: It soon became clear that this was one of the greatest archaeological discoveries ever made.
column2: 人们很快认识到，这是有史以来最重大的考古发现之一。

column1: The origin of the Dead Sea Scrolls, which were written around 2,000 years ago between 150 BCE and 70 CE, is still the subject of scholarly debate even today.
column2: 死海古卷大约写于两千年前，即公元前150年至公元70年之间，关于其来历的学术争论至今仍在继续。

column1: According to the prevailing theory, they are the work of a population that inhabited the area until Roman troops destroyed the settlement around 70 CE.
column2: 根据目前最普遍的说法，古卷出自当地居民之手。这些人一直住在这里，直到罗马军队在公元70年前后摧毁这个聚落。
column3: prevailing theory|占主导地位的理论

column1: The area was known as Judea at that time, and the people are thought to have belonged to a group called the Essenes, a devout Jewish sect.
column2: 这个地区当时叫犹太地。人们认为，这些居民属于一个名为艾赛尼派的群体，是犹太教的一个虔诚信仰派别。

column1: The majority of the texts on the Dead Sea Scrolls are in Hebrew, with some fragments written in an ancient version of its alphabet thought to have fallen out of use in the fifth century BCE.
column2: 死海古卷的文字大多是希伯来语，其中一些残片用的是古希伯来字母。据推测，这套古字母早在公元前5世纪就已停用。
column9: fallen out of use|不再使用

column1: But there are other languages as well.
column2: 不过，卷中也有其他语言。

column1: Some scrolls are in Aramaic, the language spoken by many inhabitants of the region from the sixth century BCE to the siege of Jerusalem in 70 CE.
column2: 有些卷轴用阿拉米语写成。从公元前6世纪到公元70年耶路撒冷被围困之时，当地许多居民说的都是这种语言。

column1: In addition, several texts feature translations of the Hebrew Bible into Greek.
column2: 此外，还有几篇文本是《希伯来圣经》的希腊语译文。

column1: The Dead Sea Scrolls include fragments from every book of the Old Testament of the Bible except for the Book of Esther.
column2: 死海古卷包含《圣经》旧约各卷的残片，只有《以斯帖记》例外。

column1: The only entire book of the Hebrew Bible preserved among the manuscripts from Qumran is Isaiah; this copy, dated to the first century BCE, is considered the earliest biblical manuscript still in existence.
column2: 昆兰出土的手稿中，《希伯来圣经》只有《以赛亚书》整部保存下来。这份抄本写于公元前1世纪，被视为现存最早的《圣经》手稿。

column1: Along with biblical texts, the scrolls include documents about sectarian regulations and religious writings that do not appear in the Old Testament.
column2: 除《圣经》文本外，古卷还收录了有关教派规章的文献，以及一些未见于《旧约》的宗教著作。

column1: The writing on the Dead Sea Scrolls is mostly in black or occasionally red ink, and the scrolls themselves are nearly all made of either parchment (animal skin) or an early form of paper called ‘papyrus’.
column2: 死海古卷上的字迹多用黑墨写成，偶尔也用红墨。卷轴本身几乎全用羊皮纸（兽皮）或一种名叫莎草纸的早期纸张制成。

column1: The only exception is the scroll numbered 3Q15, which was created out of a combination of copper and tin.
column2: 唯一的例外是编号为3Q15的卷轴，它由铜和锡混合制成。

column1: Known as the Copper Scroll, this curious document features letters chiselled onto metal — perhaps, as some have theorized, to better withstand the passage of time.
column2: 这份别具一格的文献就是“铜卷”，其文字凿刻在金属上。有人推测，这或许是为了使文字更能经受岁月的侵蚀。

column1: One of the most intriguing manuscripts from Qumran, this is a sort of ancient treasure map that lists dozens of gold and silver caches.
column2: 这是昆兰出土的最耐人寻味的手稿之一，像一幅古代藏宝图，列出了几十处金银窖藏。

column1: Using an unconventional vocabulary and odd spelling, it describes 64 underground hiding places that supposedly contain riches buried for safekeeping.
column2: 铜卷采用不寻常的词语和奇特的拼法，描述了64处地下藏匿点，据说里面埋有为求安全而藏起的财宝。

column1: None of these hoards have been recovered, possibly because the Romans pillaged Judea during the first century CE.
column2: 这些窖藏无一被寻获，可能是因为罗马人曾在公元1世纪劫掠犹太地。

column1: According to various hypotheses, the treasure belonged to local people, or was rescued from the Second Temple before its destruction or never existed to begin with.
column2: 关于这些财宝有不同假说：可能是当地人所有，可能是在第二圣殿被毁前从中抢救出来的，也可能从一开始就不存在。

column1: Some of the Dead Sea Scrolls have been on interesting journeys.
column2: 有些死海古卷还经历过颇为有趣的辗转流传。

column1: In 1948, a Syrian Orthodox archbishop known as Mar Samuel acquired four of the original seven scrolls from a Jerusalem shoemaker and part-time antiquity dealer, paying less than $100 for them.
column2: 1948年，叙利亚正教会的一位大主教，人称马尔·塞缪尔，从耶路撒冷一名兼做古董买卖的鞋匠手中，以不到100美元的价格，买下了最初七卷古卷中的四卷。

column1: He then travelled to the United States and unsuccessfully offered them to a number of universities, including Yale.
column2: 此后，他前往美国，试着把古卷卖给包括耶鲁大学在内的多所大学，却没有成功。

column1: Finally, in 1954, he placed an advertisement in the business newspaper The Wall Street Journal — under the category ‘Miscellaneous Items for Sale’ — that read: ‘Biblical Manuscripts dating back to at least 200 B.C. are for sale.
column2: 最终，在1954年，他在财经报纸《华尔街日报》的“杂项物品出售”栏下登了一则广告，上面写道：“现有《圣经》手稿出售，其年代至少可追溯至公元前200年。

column1: This would be an ideal gift to an educational or religious institution by an individual or group.’
column2: 个人或团体若要向教育或宗教机构馈赠礼物，这将是理想之选。”

column1: Fortunately, Israeli archaeologist and statesman Yigael Yadin negotiated their purchase and brought the scrolls back to Jerusalem, where they remain to this day.
column2: 幸运的是，以色列考古学家、政治家伊加尔·亚丁出面商谈，买下了这些古卷并将其带回耶路撒冷。它们至今仍保存在那里。

column1: In 2017, researchers from the University of Haifa restored and deciphered one of the last untranslated scrolls.
column2: 2017年，海法大学的研究人员修复并破解了当时仅剩的几卷尚未翻译的古卷之一。

column1: The university’s Eshbal Ratson and Jonathan Ben-Dov spent one year reassembling the 60 fragments that make up the scroll.
column2: 海法大学的埃什巴尔·拉特松和乔纳森·本-多夫花了一年时间，将构成这卷古卷的60块残片重新拼合。

column1: Deciphered from a band of coded text on parchment, the find provides insight into the community of people who wrote it and the 364-day calendar they would have used.
column2: 这项发现来自对羊皮纸上一段编码文字的破译，使人得以了解书写古卷的群体，以及他们当时应当采用的364天历法。
column7: provides insight into|使人深入了解

column1: The scroll names celebrations that indicate shifts in seasons and details two yearly religious events known from another Dead Sea Scroll.
column2: 古卷列出了标志季节转换的庆典名称，还详细记载了两项一年一度的宗教活动；人们从另一卷死海古卷中也知道这两项活动。

column1: Only one more known scroll remains untranslated.
column2: 已知的古卷中，只剩一卷尚未翻译。
